title: Phishing
overview: Review a suspicious email link through mail-gateway and URL inspection signals.
prerequisites: Read the baseline and compare event fields. No external tools are required.

attack.name: Spearphishing Link
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: A credential-lure verdict and failed sender alignment on the same inspected link justify reviewing the message.
evidence: Check the recipient, sender alignment, URL verdict and destination domain. Keep the domain as evidence text.
false_positive: Legitimate forwarded mail can fail alignment. Use independent URL inspection before escalating.
tuning: Scope exceptions to a known sender and forwarding flow. Review the redirect and expiration of any allowlist entry.
response: Quarantine matching messages, review clicks and sign-ins, and reset sessions if the recipient entered credentials.
prevention: Enforce DMARC with SPF and DKIM, inspect URLs, and require phishing-resistant authentication.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: URL classification is supplied by the simulated gateway. The lab never contacts the destination.

options: Mailbox size and recipient display name
questions.explanation: The detection combines a lure verdict with failed sender alignment.

questions.prompt: Where do you look for account impact?
questions.explanation: A blocked message has different impact from subsequent account activity.
